ContentsHeading.description: Shown where an archive says what it holds.

DamageSettingsFor.description: Shown in the window. Carries one value, {{.Damage}}, which has to stay spelled exactly that way.

DecimalMark.description: What this language writes between the whole part of a number and its tenths, as in 10.0 MB. One character.

Defect.description: Shown in the window. Carries one value, {{.Detail}}, which has to stay spelled exactly that way.
Defect.other: Something inside the program went wrong, and it should not have. Report it with this description: {{.Detail}}

DetailBasePreset.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailBasePreset.other: The settings under it are the preset's own. One left empty takes its default, and the manifest records which ones did.

DetailBoundary.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailBoundary.other: Give the limit your system declares, as 10mb. Units count in 1024s, and the run prints the number it used.

DetailBuildOnPreset.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailBuildOnPreset.other: Unticked, the batches below are the whole recipe. Ticked, the chosen preset's files come first and the batches are added after them.

DetailDamage.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailDamage.other: The files come out the size you asked for and no reader will accept them, which is what a validator has to reject. The manifest records what was broken and says the file is expected to be rejected.

DetailDonate.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailDonate.other: Opens the support page in your browser. The tool is free and stays free - this pays for the time that goes into it.

DetailExpected.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailExpected.other: It reaches the manifest and nothing else reads it. Leave it alone where the right answer depends on the application's own policy.

DetailGroup.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailGroup.other: It reaches the manifest, so a test can assert about a whole class of case at once.

DetailLabel.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailLabel.other: Writes into the file what it is and how big it was meant to be. Turn it off for a file that has to hold nothing but its content.

DetailManifest.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailManifest.other: It goes in the output directory beside the files.

DetailNameTemplate.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailNameTemplate.other: Left empty, the files are named after the batch and numbered, like invoices_0001.pdf. Fill it in and the name is used exactly as written, extension and all. The one placeholder is {index:04}, which becomes 0001, 0002 and so on, and a batch of more than one file needs it.

DetailOutputDir.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailOutputDir.other: It is created if it is not there.

DetailPreset.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailPreset.other: The set is worked out from the answer.

DetailPurpose.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailPurpose.other: It is written into the manifest and into the instructions beside it, which say what every file of the run is for. It changes no byte of any file.

DetailReason.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailReason.other: From a closed list, so a report can group by reason. It names the rule in play whatever the outcome is - a file a byte under a size limit is expected to be accepted, and the rule in play is still the size limit. A reason needs an outcome beside it.

DetailSeed.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailSeed.other: On any machine and in any build of this tool. 0 is the seed a run uses when nobody asks for another one. It is a seed like any other rather than a request for random files, which this tool never produces.

DetailSize.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailSize.other: Units count in 1024s, so 10mb is 10485760 bytes. A plain number is a count of bytes.

DetailSizeRange.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailSizeRange.other: Two sizes with a hyphen, as 1kb-8kb. Each file gets its own size, drawn from the seed, so the run repeats.

DetailSizeWay.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailSizeWay.other: One size gives every file the same size. A range draws a different size for each file. Around a limit makes three files: one byte under the limit, one on it, one over.

DetailTargetID.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailTargetID.other: It reaches the manifest and the file names, so a test can tell these files from the rest of the run. The seeds are derived from it, so changing it changes the bytes.

DetailTool.description: The longer explanation behind the button beside a field name.
DetailTool.other: What the tool works on and its settings change with the tool chosen.

RendererDidNotHelp.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does.
RendererDidNotHelp.other: The software renderer shipped beside the program was loaded, and the graphics toolkit still could not open a window with it.

RendererDrawing.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does.
RendererDrawing.other: This window is drawn by the software renderer shipped beside the program (Mesa llvmpipe), not by the graphics driver. Everything works. Drawing is slower than with a driver that provides OpenGL 2.1.

RendererNotBeside.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does. Carries one value, {{.Path}}, which has to stay spelled exactly that way.
RendererNotBeside.other: The software renderer that ships with the Windows archive was not found beside the program - {{.Path}} is missing. Put the opengl folder from the archive back next to tfg-gui.exe, or use a graphics driver that provides OpenGL 2.1.

RendererNotLoaded.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does. Carries one value, {{.Error}}, which has to stay spelled exactly that way.
RendererNotLoaded.other: The software renderer shipped beside the program could not be loaded: {{.Error}}.

RendererNotReadable.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does. Carries one value, {{.Error}}, which has to stay spelled exactly that way.
RendererNotReadable.other: A file of the software renderer beside the program could not be read: {{.Error}}. Check who may read the opengl folder next to tfg-gui.exe, or use a graphics driver that provides OpenGL 2.1.

RendererNotShipped.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does.
RendererNotShipped.other: No software renderer ships for this system, so this flag changes nothing here.

RendererStartFailed.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does. Carries one value, {{.Error}}, which has to stay spelled exactly that way.
RendererStartFailed.other: Starting the program again with the software renderer did not work: {{.Error}}.

RendererStartingAgain.description: About the software renderer shipped beside the program on Windows: in the system dialog and on standard error when the window could not be opened even so, on standard error when a window starts drawing with it, and on the About screen while it does.
RendererStartingAgain.other: The first attempt to open a window did not succeed - usually a graphics driver without OpenGL 2.1. Starting again with the software renderer shipped beside the program.
